articles.title: Matt Leinart: Here's Why Indiana QB Josh Hoover Is A Heisman Dark Horse
articles.summary: Matt Leinart made the case for why Indiana quarterback Josh Hoover is an under-the-radar Heisman candidate.
articles.body: Indiana quarterback Josh Hoover has extended the program's winning streak to 21 games and been a smooth operator of the offense. So why isn't he getting more Heisman buzz? Matt Leinart thinks it's time to change that. "No one's talked about Josh Hoover," Leinart said on Saturday's edition of "Big Noon Kickoff." "Fernando Mendoza came out of nowhere last year toward the second half of the season [for Indiana]. Hoover's got better stats than Mendoza, hasn't turned the football over and is a really talented player. "He's got a chance with this schedule, starting today [against Nebraska] and then Ohio State next week in the Big Ten to make a run at this thing [the Heisman Trophy]." Through Indiana's first five games, Hoover, a fifth-year senior, has totaled 1,101 passing yards, 15 passing touchdowns, zero interceptions and a 203.7 passer rating, while completing 71.0% of his passes. Hoover's passing touchdowns and passer rating each lead the Big Ten. As for Indiana's offense, the Hoosiers rank second in the Big Ten in rushing yards (252.6 per game), third in both total yards (489.6 per game) and points (44.2 per game) and 11th in passing yards (237.0 per game). Hoover transferred to Indiana after four seasons at TCU, where he spent three years as the starting quarterback. From 2023-25, he posted averages of 3,209.0 passing yards, 23.7 passing touchdowns and 11.0 interceptions per season, along with a 147.8 passer rating and a 65.1% completion rate. Now, Hoover is following in the footsteps of Mendoza, who led Indiana to its first national championship in program history during a perfect 16-0 season in 2025. Mendoza threw for 3,535 yards and 41 touchdowns with six interceptions, posting a 182.9 passer rating and completing 72.0% of his passes. Mendoza also rushed for 276 yards and seven touchdowns en route to winning the 2025 Heisman Trophy. He ultimately became the No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, selected by the Las Vegas Raiders. With two unbeaten opponents in Nebraska and Ohio State looming, Hoover has a chance to put himself in the Heisman conversation. "I think he's exceeded expectations so far," Leinart added. "Obviously, the schedule picks up starting today and next week, and then in the second half of the season. But I just want to say this: I think it's time to start putting some respect on Josh Hoover's name. He's one of the best players in the country."

articles.title: El golazo de chalaca que le anularon a Luis Díaz en el empate del Bayern Múnich
articles.standfirst: El golazo de chalaca anulado a Luis Díaz en Augsburgo vs. Bayern Múnich: VIDEO
articles.summary: El golazo de chalaca anulado a Luis Díaz en Augsburgo vs. Bayern Múnich: VIDEO
articles.body: Luis Díaz sorprendió a todos en el compromiso de la Bundesliga frente al Augsburgo con un recurso acrobático espectacular. Sin embargo, un fuera de lugar privó al colombiano de celebrar uno de los mejores goles de la temporada. El futbolista guajiro Luis Díaz volvió a ser el centro de atención en el fútbol internacional durante el cruce entre el Augsburgo y el Bayern Múnich. En el inicio de la segunda parte, el atacante colombiano firmó una jugada de antología que prometía convertirse en una de las joyas de la fecha, aunque el arbitraje terminó ahogando el grito de gol. Tras irse al descanso abajo en el marcador (1-0), el Bayern Múnich salió en el complemento decidido a buscar la remontada. Fue en ese momento cuando surgió el talento de Lucho: ante un centro al área y una floja respuesta en la salida del guardameta del Augsburgo, Díaz cazó el balón en el aire y sacó una chalaca espectacular que envió el balón al fondo de la red. La plasticidad del remate provocó la admiración inmediata de compañeros y espectadores. No obstante, la euforia duró apenas unos instantes. Tras la revisión en la sala de videoarbitraje, el colegiado determinó invalidar la acción debido a una posición adelantada en la fase previa del ataque. La posición irregular al comienzo de la jugada dejó sin validez la genialidad del guajiro. A pesar del trago amargo para el atacante guajiro, la insistencia del Bayern dio frutos poco después. Instantes más tarde, el marroquí Ismael Saibari aprovechó una nueva oportunidad en ataque para decretar la igualdad 1-1 definitiva en el marcador, devolviéndole la tranquilidad al conjunto bávaro.

articles.title: PDC Women's Series: Fallon Sherrock and Gemma Hayter qualify for World Championship as Beau Greaves sweeps up with Events 21-22 in Wigan
articles.summary: Beau Greaves continues her monopoly of the PDC Women's Series, defeating Vicky Pruim in the Event 21 decider and Gemma Hayter 5-3 to claim the Event 22 title; you can watch the Grand Slam of Darts in Wolverhampton live on Sky Sports from November 14-22
articles.body:
'The Queen of the Palace' will return to the place where she wrote history in 2020, after she confirmed her spot in the top five of the Women's Series.

Sherrock became the first (and only) woman to pick up wins at Alexandra Palace, beating Ted Evetts and Mensur Suljovic before losing to Chris Dobey.

She has since returned five times but came up fruitless against the likes of Steve Beaton, Ricky Evans, Jermaine Wattimena, Ryan Meikle and Dave Chisnall.

She will make her seventh appearance in December, despite only picking up one title so far on the Women's Series.

Hayter's run to the Event 22 final was enough to confirm her World Championship return.

Hayter qualified after reaching her third final of the year; she is now confirmed to finish in the top five on the Women's Series Order of Merit, hence booking her spot at a second World Championship.

She lost on debut to Josh Rock last year but took a set in a good performance.

She also picked up the WDF World Masters Title in 2026, as well as her first win at the Women's World Matchplay.

Hayter will be joined at Alexandra Palace by Lisa Ashton, Sherrock and Greaves, with Vicky Pruim currently in pole position to claim the final qualification spot via the PDC Women's Series rankings.

Greaves continued her PDC Women's Series domination with another brace of titles in Wigan on Saturday.

The reigning three-time Women's World Matchplay champion claimed back-to-back titles on a bumper day of action, as the year's final weekend of Women's Series action got under way at the Robin Park Leisure Centre.

'Beau 'n' Arrow' breezed to the Event 21 title in emphatic style, conceding just five legs in scooping her 14th title of the campaign.

The Doncaster superstar opened her challenge with successive whitewash wins against Laura van den Berg and Ruby Grey, before overcoming Dutch star Aileen de Graaf in round three.

Greaves then averaged north of 101 in a sensational quarter-final blitz of Rhian O'Sullivan, which she backed up with a five-leg drubbing of Sherrock in the semi-finals.

This set up a winner-takes-all showdown against Sweden's Pruim in the Event 21 showpiece, which saw Greaves fire in a superb 13-darter to wrap up a hard-fought 5-3 success.

Greaves extended her winning run with comfortable wins over Sharon Godbeer and Gemma Reynolds in the early stages of Event 22, before recovering from 3-1 down to deny Lisa Ashton.

Ashton squandered multiple match darts to complete a 4-1 win, and after frittering away further opportunities in a last-leg decider, she was duly punished by a ruthless Greaves.

The World Youth Championship runner-up then swept aside Steph Clarke, Joanne Oldershaw and Leanne Topper to maintain her charge, which set up a fascinating clash against Gemma Hayter for the Event 22 crown.

There was little to separate the pair for large periods of the contest, but Greaves eventually prevailed in a high-quality affair, overcoming some late double trouble to celebrate her record-extending 61st Women's Series title.

Despite missing out on a first title of 2026, Hayter's run to the Event 22 final was enough to confirm her Ally Pally return.

Ashton, meanwhile, will also feature in next month's Mr Vegas Grand Slam of Darts, with the Lancashire stalwart now assured of a second-place finish on the Women's Series rankings.

The 2026 PDC Women's Series season will culminate with Events 23-24 in Wigan on Sunday.

articles.title: Minnesota Vikings bring Odell Beckham Jr. up from practice squad for game against Saints
articles.summary: Odell Beckham Jr. gets elevated from the Minnesota Vikings practice squad with Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison both listed as questionable.
articles.body: While his return to New York didn't exactly pan out, Odell Beckham Jr. is already getting a chance to show what he can do in the NFL after signing with the Minnesota Vikings' practice squad. Or, at least he can show what he can do standing on the sideline with pads on. It's been reported that the team is elevating the veteran wide receiver from the practice squad ahead of this week's game against the New Orleans Saints. ODELL BECKHAM JR LAMENTS HIS SHORT-LIVED RETURN TO THE NEW YORK GIANTS: 'I SHOULD HAVE KNOWN BETTER' That doesn't mean Beckham will see any game action, but it gives the Vikings options if they're without top wide receivers Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison, both listed as questionable. The 11-year NFL veteran out of LSU hasn't logged a single reception this season and was only targeted once in three games with the Giants. EX-NFL STAR BELIEVES ODELL BECKHAM JR 'STILL BETTER THAN MOST OF THE RECEIVERS' IN NFL AS HE RETURNS TO GIANTS But, hey, the warm-up highlights were electrifying! Jefferson is dealing with an ankle issue, while Addison has a hamstring injury. According to ESPN, head coach Kevin O'Connell indicated that Jefferson — who has been out of action since late September — is headed in the right direction. "He progressed throughout the week," he said. "So much of it is just how he feels after getting some work today. And we still have quite a bit of time between the rest of the day, tomorrow, and obviously into game day to make that determination based upon what's best for our football team and Justin." articles.title: Tulsa's David Wells Jr. tips ball to himself for improbable touchdown in wild play against Navy
articles.summary: Tulsa's Oran Singleton Jr. escaped a tackle and heaved a prayer that led to one of the wildest college football touchdowns of the season against Navy.

articles.title: WWE Money in the Bank 2026 Winners, Live Grades, Reaction and Highlights
articles.summary: WWE Money in the Bank is one of the most popular and unpredictable events on the professional wrestling calendar, and its 2026 edition took over Smoothie King Center on Saturday night.
articles.body:
WWE Money in the Bank is one of the most popular and unpredictable events on the professional wrestling calendar, and its 2026 edition took over Smoothie King Center on Saturday night.

Featuring the men's and women's namesake ladder matches, as well as Roman Reigns' World Heavyweight Championship defense, the event promised noteworthy moments that could advance ongoing storylines and launch new ones.

What went down, how did each match rate, and what impact will the results have on WWE moving forward?

Find out with this recap of the October 10 premium live event.

Men's Money in the Bank ladder match: CM Punk vs. Penta vs. Je'Von Evans vs. Kevin Owens vs. Trick Williams vs. Bron Breakker

Women's Money in the Bank ladder match: Lola Vice vs. Sol Ruca vs. Tiffany Stratton vs. Lash Legend vs. Roxanne Perez vs. Jacy Jayne

World Heavyweight Championship: LA Knight vs. Roman Reigns (c)

Women's World Championship: Stephanie Vaquer (c) vs. Becky Lynch vs. Liv Morgan

World Heavyweight Championship Match: LA Knight vs. Roman Reigns

Last Time in Action: LA Knight and Solo Sikoa fought The Usos to a No Contest (Raw, August 24); Roman Reigns defeated Penta (Raw, September 14)

LA Knight entered Saturday's World Heavyweight Championship Match against Roman Reigns with his legacy on the line. A win, and he would have paid off his journey to the top of the pro wrestling industry. A loss would make the questions about his ability to win the top prize deafening.

The Megastar threw everything he had at Reigns, driving him through the timekeeper's position and powerbombing him through a table. He countered a spear into a BFT in one of the best spots of the entire match and even perfectly executed the unnecessarily fancy top-rope jumps he is known for.

He did everything he could to put Reigns away, and survived nearly everything the OTC threw at him, but on this night in the Big Easy, he came up just short.

With desperation setting in late, Reigns crotched Knight on the top rope, then uncorked three Superman Punches. A spear followed, and the Tribal Chief retained his title.

Afterward, the 946's Bronco Nima, Lucien Price, and Royce Keys taunted Reigns from the stands, only to be confronted by The Usos and Solo Sikoa, who brawled them out of the arena and into a waiting vehicle, which sped the heels away in retreat.

Reigns defeated Knight to retain the title

The crowd in New Orleans, at least over the ESPN airwaves, was as behind LA Knight as anyone has been over the last two years. A loss here would seemingly hurt that momentum and, potentially, do irreparable damage. After all, for how long are they willing to continue supporting a guy who can never get the job done?

Corey Graves and Michael Cole did a fantastic job on commentary of putting over the enormity of Knight's moment. Win and he pays off the journey. Lose and he may never be the same again. Great work by the voices of the show.

The entire WWE Universe held its collective breath as Knight executed his jump to the top rope and superplexed Reigns to the mat.

The false finishes in this match were nothing short of fantastic, especially after the powerbomb through the table and the proceeding kickout from the Tribal Chief.

This was an outstanding match, far better than their first encounter, and further evidence that Reigns is on a generational run during this stint with the gold. Another killer match that had the fans all the way invested.

Last Time in Action: Jacy Jayne, Lash Legend, and Tiffany Stratton defeated Sol Ruca, Lola Vice, and Roxanne Perez (SmackDown, October 9)

Four first-timers, a second-time participant, and a previous winner made up the freshest field in recent Money in the Bank memory as Jayne, Legend, Vice, and Ruca competed for a chance to win the coveted briefcase for the first time.

Perez sought her first win in two tries, and Stratton attempted to make history as the second woman to win two times.

In the end, it was Tiffy Time in New Orleans as the former WWE Women's Champion secured the briefcase and etched her name in the history books. Before she outlasted Legend to win the match, fans were treated to some big bumps, some scary near-misses, and a look at the bright future of the women's division.

Legend took some big bumps, Jayne and Vice barely escaped disaster after a ladder bridge failed, Ruca stunned the WWE fans with a phenomenal frog splash, and Perez had victory within reach before an unfortunate Sol Snatcher eliminated her from the final moments.

Stratton overcame a rough early-match landing to win the briefcase and instantly create drama over on SmackDown, where her new bestie, Chelsea Green, is the reigning WWE Women's Champion.

After she was established as the most physically dominant competitor on last night's SmackDown, Legend caught a beatdown at the start of Saturday's match, a logical and smart start to the match.

"Let's face it: Lash Legend just kicked Roxanne Perez in the soul," Graves said after one of the damnedest we pump kicks in recent memory sent a step ladder back at The Prodigy's upper body.

This was easily the most athletically gifted field in Women's Money in the Bank Ladder Match history, which made for some creative and unique spots. It was also the least experienced, which meant some of those spots landed and some did not.

The camera angle on Ruca's frog splash from the top rope, to Legend and through a ladder at ringside was a big production win for WWE. It made an already incredible spot that much more awe-inspiring.

The crowd was totally behind Perez from the moment she entered the arena and even more so with every teased close call.

An energetic, action-packed match that did not overstay its welcome and featured some eyebrow-raising performances from women who will form the foundation of the division for years to come, this was a great showcase with some big spots and a surprising finish considering who most expected to win.

articles.title: Egoitz Bijueska, doble oro mundial adolescente
articles.standfirst: Gana brillantemente los World Skate Games, siempre con más de 90 puntos
articles.summary: Gana brillantemente los World Skate Games, siempre con más de 90 puntos
articles.body: Egoitz Bijueska cumplirá 16 años el 24 de noviembre pero ya es doble campeón del mundo. El adolescente vasco se proclamó en la primera mitad de la temporada campeón del World Skate en Río de Janeiro y la ha culminado ganando en Asunción (Paraguay) los World Skate Games en la modalidad de park, y además exhibiendo una impresionante solidez: en las rondas previas realizó unas excelentes puntuaciones de 94,33 en cuartos y 94,60 en semifinales. Sólo pudo superarle Tate Carew (95,00), que luego en la final no tuvo su día. Egoitz empezó la final con 93,04 puntos y en su segundo intento los mejoró: 94,50. En la modalidad lo que cuenta es exclusivamente el mejor intento de cada competidor, de modo que nadie puede estar seguro hasta el último momento. Con todo, Bijueska podía estar bastante seguro de tener plaza para la ronda final, reservada a los cinco mejores de los ocho finalistas. Tom Schaar, que a sus 27 años era el más veterano de la competición, fue el único que logró acosarle tras sus dos primeras actividades, pero se quedó en 93,07 puntos que acabarían dándole la plata. El brasileño Gui Khury, con 92,15, se colgó el bronce. En la ronda final Carew, que se enganchó a ella en el último recorrido tras fallar en los dos primeros, se cayó también, al igual que Augusto Akio y Khury. Schaar no logró superar sus 93,07, de modo que Egoitz era campeón antes de realizar la bajada final que, de todas formas, ejecutó y completó. Además de los dos títulos mundiales logrados este año, Bijueska ha sumado oro, plata y bronce en los X Games. Y, evidentemente, toma un importante impulso en el ranking olímpico, para el que esta competición era puntuable. En la final femenina Naia Laso era tercera en la primera salida a pista, pero luego no logró completar su secuencia de trucos y superar su 78,83. Al final, quinta, con Mikuzo Hasegawa, Sky Brown -que tiene ya 19 años tras haber sido oro olímpico a los 13- y Cocona Hiraki en el podio.

articles.title: Roman Reigns Beats LA Knight to Retain WWE World Title at Money in the Bank as Brawl Ensues
articles.summary: Roman Reigns defeated LA Knight at WWE Money in the Bank on Saturday to retain the World Heavyweight Championship.
articles.body:
Roman Reigns defeated LA Knight at WWE Money in the Bank on Saturday to retain the World Heavyweight Championship.

Both men had a host of near-falls in this closely contested match, which featured a confident challenger in Knight.

Reigns' Superman Punch nearly drew a three-count. Knight fought back with a Superplex-Burning Hammer combo, but that wasn't good enough either.

Reigns fought back and hit The Megastar with a uranage, but it wasn't enough to put Knight away.

The two men traded blows outside the ring and narrowly avoided a double count-out, both rushing back into the ring just in time.

Reigns then hit Knight with another Superman Punch to set him up for the spear, but the challenger countered with a BFT. Knight went for the pin, but The Tribal Chief kicked out just in time again.

The Megastar attempted a spear, but Reigns countered with his own. Another pin attempt led to another near-fall, but it wasn't enough.

Reigns then hit Knight with some heavy right hands. He dedicated each punch to a member of the Bloodline as the sequence went on, with Solo Sikoa being the last one.

But Knight hit Reigns with another spear. Another pin attempt led to another near-fall.

Knight sent Reigns through the ringside barricade after Reigns' spear attempt. He then powerbombed Reigns through the announce table, threw him into the ring and connected with a top-rope elbow drop. Somehow, that still wasn't enough to secure the pinfall.

The closing sequence began when Reigns crotched Knight on the top rope. The OTC then hit two Superman punches and a spear on his opponent, and that got the job done.

After the match, The 946 appeared in the crowd and gestured at Reigns, who didn't seem all that alarmed. Fans found out why as Solo Sikoa and The Usos soon appeared behind them.

A massive brawl ensued, and the fight went from the crowd to the concourse to outside the arena. Jaida Parker appeared in a getaway car to take The 946 away.

There is a great deal of history between Reigns and Knight dating back multiple years, and Money in the Bank marked the latest chapter in their long-running rivalry.

Despite his past issues with The Bloodline, Knight found common ground with The Usos leading up to WrestleMania 42 earlier this year, and he even teamed with them in a winning effort against Logan Paul, Austin Theory and IShowSpeed.

However, after Reigns beat CM Punk for the world heavyweight title in the main event of WrestleMania, The Usos aligned with their cousin once again and reformed The Bloodline, much to the chagrin of Knight.

After having seen The Bloodline run roughshod over WWE in the past and cost him the chance to become world champ multiple times in 2023 and 2024, Knight had no interest in seeing The Bloodline back in power.

In the weeks and months that followed, Knight expressed his concerns about The Bloodline to Raw general manager Adam Pearce on multiple occasions, and attempted to convince The Usos to leave the group in the past.

When his efforts fell flat, The Megastar found some unexpected allies in Sikoa and Royce Keys, both of whom were at odds with The Bloodline as well.

Knight, Sikoa and Keys teamed up to beat The Usos and Jacob Fatu at SummerSlam, allowing The Megastar to build more momentum toward a world title opportunity.

While Knight accused Reigns of ducking him due to the fact that he agreed to face the winner of a tournament made up entirely of luchadores in a world title match in Mexico City, his chance finally came.

After Reigns beat Penta on Raw in Mexico City last month, Knight attacked Reigns, and his World Heavyweight Championship bout against The Tribal Chief was made official for Money in the Bank shortly thereafter.

Although Knight had plenty of motivation and crowd support behind him, The OTC prevailed and once again denied The Megastar what would have been his first world title win in WWE.

articles.title: How Hope volleyball knocked off No. 1 Wisconsin-Oshkosh in epic five-set battle
articles.summary: Huge plays at huge moments lead to the Flying Dutch stunning the top team in NCAA Division III.
articles.body:
Photos: Hope College vs. Adrian women’s volleyball

With a mostly new lineup, the Hope College volleyball team has shown its potential, but also has shown understandable growing pains.

Now, the entire country knows the team's potential.

Hope knocked off No. 1 Wisconsin-Oshkosh in a five-set thriller - so close that three sets went extra points - winning 26-28, 26-24, 22-25, 26-24, 15-12 on Saturday, Oct. 10, in Eau Claire, Wisconsin.

Leading 11-10 in the fifth set, Hope's Kiera Morrison put down a kill. After Oshkosh scored a point, Morrison put down another kill to make it 14-11. Two points later, Morrison again put down a kill, this time on match point, to secure the 15-12 win.

The second set was pivotal for the Flying Dutch, which lost to No. 4 Eau Claire and beat Wisconsin-Superior earlier in the Wisconsin-Eau Claire Tournament.

After losing the first set in extra points, the second set went into extras, too.

Morrison put down a kill to tie it 23-23. Oshkosh's Samantha Perlberg answered with a kill to earn a set point.

One more point for Oshkosh and the ending could have been very different.

But Hope middle hitter Kamryn Burbridge slammed a kill to tie it 24-24, then two attack errors from Oshkosh gave Hope the 26-24 lead - and all the momentum.

Angie Butler finished with 16 kills, while Burbridge had 15, Maddie Ostrander had 11 and Morrison put down 10 to go along with three aces. Burbridge put down eight blocks.

Setter Brooke Hehl dished out 58 assists. Kathryn Oates tallied 25 digs, while Amelia Gagnon had 18 and Hehl and Emma Flick each added 12.

Hope improved to 13-6 and will likely be back in the top 25 rankings next week. Top-ranked Oshkosh dropped to 18-2.

articles.summary: Five of Notre Dame’s touchdowns were of 30-or-more yards.
articles.body:
SOUTH BEND, Ind. — Freshman Jonaz Walton scored on a 97-yard run — the third longest offensive play in Notre Dame Stadium history — and finished with 181 yards as the No. 3 Fighting Irish routed Stanford 58-7 on Saturday.

Walton's 181 yards are the most by a Notre Dame running back this season. Walton also scored on a 40-yard run against Stanford.

The only longer offensive plays at Notre Dame Stadium besides Walton's 97-yard run belong to Josh Adams (2015 vs. Wake Forest) and Jeremiyah Love (2024 vs. Indiana). Each had 98-yard scoring runs.

Notre Dame (6-0) extended its overall winning streak to 16 games — all by double-digits. The Fighting Irish edged closer to the record of 21 consecutive double-digit victory margins set by Army (1944-46). Miami is second with 17 consecutive double-digit victories from 2000 to 2001.

Five of Notre Dame's touchdowns were of 30-or-more yards.

C.J. Carr finished with 14-of-20 passing for 181 yards and three touchdowns. He also rushed five times for 41 yards.

Aneyas Williams rushed seven times for 28 yards, but scored on a 70-yard pass from Carr. Nolan James Jr. carried the ball 10 times for 73 yards and two touchdowns.

Notre Dame's defense set a tone in the first 12 seconds. Boubacar Traore sacked Stanford quarterback Davis Warren and forced a fumble recovered by Jaiden Ausberry. Two plays later, James scored from the 3 at the 14:07 mark of the first quarter.

Traore also had an interception and a tackle for loss.

Stanford (2-4) scored in the third quarter. A 52-yard rocket from Warren to Caden High set up a three-yard TD strike from Warren to Benji Blackburn.

The Cardinal road losing streak is now 14 games — the longest road losing streak in the nation, tied with Ball State. Stanford has been outscored 115-10 in its last two games.

BYU is 5-0 and coming off a 24-10 Friday night home win over Iowa State. Notre Dame, meanwhile, hasn't been challenged much on their way to a 6-0 start. This will be the first ranked both teams have played this season.

Notre Dame will likely be a double-digit favorite and has future NFL talent all over the field. Notre Dame has won all six games by double digits, although Michigan State and North Carolina were semi-competitive with the Irish for the chunk of their games.

This is the time in program history BYU will be ranked in the top 10 and host a top 10 team. The game kicks off Saturday, October 17 at 5:30 MT on ABC.

articles.title: No. 9 Ole Miss routs Vanderbilt 52-17 behind 4 combined TDs from Trinidad Chambliss
articles.summary: (AP) — Trinidad Chambliss threw for 213 yards and three touchdowns and ran for another score as ninth-ranked Mississippi routed Vanderbilt 52-17 on Saturday....
articles.body:
NASHVILLE, Tenn. (AP) — Trinidad Chambliss threw for 213 yards and three touchdowns and ran for another score as ninth-ranked Mississippi routed Vanderbilt 52-17 on Saturday.

The Rebels (4-1, 2-1 Southeastern Conference) notched their sixth straight win and 10th in 12 over Vanderbilt (3-3, 0-3). Chambliss put them ahead to stay with a 10-yard touchdown run as Ole Miss scored on four straight drives in the first half for a 42-3 halftime lead.

The Rebels scored 24 points off four turnovers. Suntarine Perkins had one of three sacks for Ole Miss, and he returned a fumble 4 yards for a TD.

Kewan Lacy started in his first game back after leaving Ole Miss' win over LSU and missed the loss to Florida. Lacy ran for a 2-yard TD and finished with 39 yards on seven carries.

For Vanderbilt , this was the program's worst loss since a 47-6 thumping Nov. 11, 2023, at South Carolina.

Freshman quarterback Jared Curtis started after an undisclosed injury kept him out of last week's loss at No. 2 Georgia. Curtis threw for 222 yards and made throws showing off the arm that made him the No. 2 overall recruit for 2026. He also was intercepted twice and fumbled when sacked by Blake Perkins near his own goal line.

Chambliss started with back-to-back incompletions on a wet day. He completed his next 11 passes for 105 yards, and Chambliss threw a 2-yard TD pass to starting nose tackle Jamarious Brown and then connected with Deuce Alexander for a 39-yard catch-and-run for a TD with 4:41 left and a 28-3 lead.

His 4-yard TD pass to Michael Smith after a lost fumble on a kickoff return put Ole Miss up 42-3 at halftime.

Mississippi: Coach Pete Golding planned to rotate Lacy and ease him back in from the injury. The Rebels made that easy with how Chambliss moved them up and down the field. Seven different Rebels carried the ball, and nine different Rebels caught at least one pass.

Vanderbilt: The Commodores aren't good enough not to cost themselves with untimely penalties and mistakes. A personal foul on lineman Clinton Azubuike after a run set up second-and-goal at the Ole Miss 2 into a 45-yard field goal by Brock Taylor. Curtis wasn't ready for a shotgun snap that hit his face mask on second-and-1, a fumble the Commodores recovered. They had five penalties for 59 yards in the first quarter alone only to finish with 11 for 92.

articles.title: Grading UConn football's performance in road win at Temple
articles.summary: UConn’s offense rushes for 248 yards to earn a bounce back win at Temple.
articles.body:
UConn football got a much-needed bounce back win Saturday, Oct. 10.

Following two heartbreaking losses to Miami (Ohio) and Syracuse, the Huskies went on the road and defeated Temple 34-20 to snap its skid.

UConn totaled 248 yards on the ground in the win. An eight-yard rush from Cyncir Bowers early in the fourth quarter all but sealed the win for UConn, which improved to 3-3 going into its bye week.

Here's how we graded the Huskies' performance.

The offense started off hot, scoring on four of its first five drives of the game.

Quarterback Kalieb Osborne had one of his more efficient games of the season as he completed 17 of 23 passes for 257 yards.

UConn got a complete performance from its running back room as the trio of Kenji Christian, Cyncir Bowers and Trey Cornist combined for 237 yards and three touchdowns on 26 touches.

But some of the same problems that occurred over the last two weeks reared its ugly head again on Saturday. The offense stalled for much of the third quarter, allowing Temple chances at breaking the game open.

Still, Osborne and the offense were efficient in big spots, which is all you can ask for from a young team at this point in the season.

Despite giving up a few huge plays, the Huskies stayed solid for a majority of the afternoon.

UConn forced two turnovers as Shamar Riser-Pressley and Renick Dorilas each recorded a forced fumble. Temple's high-powered rushing attack finished with 146 yards after averaging just over 212 yards per game over the last five contests.

The Huskies brought down quarterback Ajani Sheppard four times.

Nothing spectacular, but a solid showing from the special team's unit. Kicker Jack O'Connor scored field goals from 21 and 27 yards out. He hit all four of his extra-point attempts.

After two heartbreaking losses, Jason Candle and his staff bounced back in a big way.

When the Huskies had the lead in the fourth quarter, Candle didn't play it safe. Instead, he let Osborne and the offense continue to try and move the ball forward.

The offense stalled in the third quarter, but the coaching staff pushed all the right buttons to come away with a big win on the road.

Notably, penalties were still an issue with UConn, committing eight infractions that resulted in 65 yards.

UConn finally got a complete game running the ball, and it was a group effort.

Cyncir Bowers carried the ball 18 times for 84 yards. Trey Cornist rushed for 114 yards on seven carries, Kenji Christian totaled 39 yards on just one touch and Osborne had 11 yards. All four had a touchdown rush.

articles.title: Michigan State football injuries spread to LBs in OT loss to Illinois
articles.summary: Michigan State football score: A seemingly game-changing onside kick was negated in the fourth quarter as the Spartans lost to Illinois in overtime.
articles.body:
EAST LANSING – Even a date with one of the Big Ten's worst defenses wasn't enough to solve Michigan State football 's malaise on offense for three quarters.

And then, in the fourth, boom: The Spartans rallied from a 14-point fourth quarter deficit. But it was for naught, as MSU failed to get a 2-point conversion in OT, resulting in a 38-37 overtime loss at Spartan Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 10.

Making matters worse, injuries continued to decimate the MSU defense, with three key linebackers – Jordan Hall, Brady Pretzlaff and Dion Crawford – knocked out of the game with various injuries. MSU (2-4, 0-3 Big Ten) won't have much time to get healthy, either, with two games yet to play before it gets its bye week on Oct. 31.

MSU QB Alessio Milivojevic was efficient in passing for two touchdowns, but couldn't get the Spartans into the end zone one final time in OT. Katin Houser, his counterpart in orange making his first return to Spartan Stadium after two seasons at MSU and two others at East Carolina , led several long drives and completed nearly 75% of his passes, accounting for a touchdown through the air and on the ground.

Houser didn't finish the game, however, suffering what appeared to be an injury on his throwing hand while making a tackle on an interception return. The pick, followed one play later by Jaziun Patterson's 11-yard TD rush, got the Spartans within six points of the Illini, but that was as close as they would get.

Michigan State surprised the Illini with an onside kick after scoring a TD with 7:47 left, with freshman Samson Gash (of Novi Detroit Catholic Central) recovering the kick in Illinois territory. But the referees called Gash offsides on the play despite video evidence showing he was not .

The FS1 broadcast said the penalty was not reviewable, but the referees later announced an official review on whether Gash recovered the ball in bounds or not. That replay didn't determine whether the Spartans got the ball, but where the offsides penalty would apply.

Since Gash was ruled to have recovered the ball in-bounds, Michigan State got to re-kick, even though the referees initially reviewed the opposite.

It was a confusing few minutes for Michigan State, whose fans celebrated upon review despite not knowing that Gash's recovery would not count.

Just about everything that could go wrong for MSU did go wrong in the first quarter against Illinois (3-3, 1-2).

On offense, the Spartans suffered a pair of three-and-outs, gaining just 8 yards total. That started with a daring call on the opening play – a flea-flicker that had a pair of receivers open deep … crushed by a sack of Milivojevic as the Illini sliced through the Spartans' line.

Things didn't get much better for the defense, which surrendered 10 points, eight first downs, and 115 yards passing to Houser as Illinois marched 54 yards in seven plays for a field goal on its first drive and then 80 yards on 12 plays for a touchdown.

Making matters worse: MSU lost its two best linebackers, as Hall – returned Saturday after missing last week's game – departed with an apparent shoulder injury, and Pretzlaff exited after going down hard on his neck and shoulder.

After that dismal first quarter, the Spartans finally found some answers on offense in the second. First up: Their first first down, which game with 8:14 left before the half. That came on the second play of the drive, on a 9-yard run by Jaziun Patterson. Nine plays after that, MSU was finally back in the endzone, for the first time in eight quarters – two against Nebraska two weeks ago, all four vs. Wisconsin last week, and the first quarter on Saturday – ending a TD drought of 122 minutes, 38 seconds of game time.

Petterson was the hero on the TD, too, hauling in a pass in the flat from Milivojevic and racing to the right pylon for a 6-yard score to make it a 17-7 game.

It won't be homecoming week, but it will be a coming home for quarterback Aidan Chiles, who spent his previous two seasons in East Lansing under center with former MSU coach Jonathan Smith. Now with Northwestern (4-1, 1-1 Big Ten), Chiles has thrived in the exotic schemes of new NU offensive coordinator Chip Kelly, completing 70.8% of his passes for 900 yards, six TDs and no interceptions while rushing for five TDs. Saturday brought more of the same in the Wildcats' rout of Ball State, as Chiles passed for 272 yards and three TDs and added another on the ground. The Wildcats and Spartans will have an early start on Saturday, Oct. 17, with kickoff set for noon on Peacock (streaming only).

articles.title: ESPN College GameDay Week 7 location announced, breaks 17-year hiatus
articles.summary: ESPN’s flagship pregame show returns to a campus it has visited once in its history, setting up a prime-time clash between two unbeaten Playoff contenders.
articles.body:
ESPN's College GameDay is heading to Provo, Utah, for Week 7, bringing the flagship pregame show to BYU for the first time in 17 years for a matchup between two unbeaten College Football Playoff contenders.

The show announced Saturday night that it will broadcast from campus before No. 3 Notre Dame visits No. 8 BYU on Oct. 17 at 7:30 p.m. ET on ABC. GameDay's only previous trip to Provo came on Oct. 24, 2009, when TCU beat BYU 38-7.

"Cougar fans, it's been awhile," the show's official account posted shortly after 7 p.m. ET, confirming the crew is "headed to Provo for the first time since 2009 for Notre Dame-BYU."

BYU Cougars defensive tackle John Taumoepeau (55) and Cosmo the Cougar celebrate after the Cougars beat the Iowa State Cyclones | Reese Strickland-Imagn Images

ESPN host Rece Davis floated BYU as the likely destination on the Sept. 28 episode of the College GameDay podcast, though he made clear the network hadn't settled on a site.

"I'm not trying to give away secrets, no decision has been made, but there's a really good chance we'll be at BYU ," Davis said.

Davis added that the matchup "might be the best game of the weekend." Provo won out over a crowded Oct. 17 slate that includes Ohio State at Indiana, a rematch of last season's Big Ten title game, along with Florida at Texas and Alabama at Tennessee.

The kickoff also lands in ABC's prime-time window. Notre Dame's home games air exclusively on NBC, so a trip to Provo gives ESPN a full Saturday of coverage built around the Irish. The visit comes one week after GameDay set up inside Coleman Coliseum for Georgia at Alabama .

The Irish moved to 6-0 with a 58-7 rout of Stanford on Saturday afternoon in South Bend, Indiana. Notre Dame coach Marcus Freeman's team led 37-0 at halftime.

BYU improved to 5-0, 3-0 in Big 12 play, with a 24-10 win over Iowa State on Friday night. Sophomore quarterback Bear Bachmeier threw for a season-high 329 yards and two touchdowns and ran for a career-high 109 yards. The Cougars are 5-0 for a third straight season , a first in program history.

BYU coach Kalani Sitake's defense held the Cyclones to 200 total yards and 2 of 13 on third down. Still, the Cougars will face the Irish without running back LJ Martin, the reigning Big 12 Offensive Player of the Year, who is reportedly out 4-6 weeks with an ankle injury .

BYU Cougars quarterback Bear Bachmeier (47) instructs the team against the Arizona Wildcats | Rob Gray-Imagn Images

Notre Dame leads the all-time series 7-2, but the Irish lost their last visit to Provo, a 20-17 BYU win in 2004. The teams last met in 2022, when Notre Dame beat BYU 28-20 in Las Vegas.

The Oct. 17 game is on track to become the first meeting of two top-10 teams in LaVell Edwards Stadium history. Both programs were the top two at-large teams left out of last season's 12-team Playoff field, and the home-and-home series replaced Notre Dame's annual game against USC. BYU returns to South Bend in 2027.

Brown came out of the backfield and caught a touchdown pass from quarterback Trinidad Chambliss in the end zone. After scoring, he hit the "Sexy Dexy" celebration that Cincinnati Bengals defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence loves.

It's a big win for Ole Miss, which will now have No. 14 Missouri coming to Oxford next week for a huge showdown. Kickoff will be at 3:30 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Tayven Jackson's 5 touchdown passes lead the way and North Texas routs Charlotte 50-10
articles.summary: DENTON, Texas (AP) — Tayven Jackson threw five touchdown passes, setting a personal best for the second consecutive game, and North Texas routed Charlotte 50...
articles.body:
DENTON, Texas (AP) — Tayven Jackson threw five touchdown passes, setting a personal best for the second consecutive game, and North Texas routed Charlotte 50-10 on Saturday.

Jackson's previous high was four touchdown passes in a 45-44 overtime win over Tulsa on Oct. 1.

On Saturday, Jackson threw four touchdown passes in the first half and Jahiem White ran 61 yards for a fifth score, leading North Texas to a 40-10 halftime lead.

Jackson's fifth TD throw, a 34-yard connection with Justin Stevenson made it 47-10 through three quarters. Jackson did not play in the fourth quarter.

The Mean Green (4-2, 2-0 American Conference) entered averaging 40.6 points per game and were the only FBS team with a top-10 passer and top-10 rusher in the nation. Jackson had 1,519 passing yards for fifth in the country and White's 582 rushing yards placed him ninth. White had 105 yards on Saturday.

Jackson completed 24 of 31 passes for 349 yards. Stevenson caught two touchdown passes for the second consecutive game and finished with 122 yards on nine total receptions. The senior transfer from Wyoming has five TDs in the last three games.

Conner Harrell threw for 218 yards for the 49ers (0-6, 0-2). He had one TD pass and threw two interceptions.

articles.title: Oregon benches Dylan Raiola as quarterback controversy begins to brew after UCLA loss
articles.summary: The Ducks only problem is not having two losses.
articles.body:
The 13th-ranked Oregon Ducks are facing growing questions about their quarterback situation after head coach Dan Lanning benched Dylan Raiola during a frustrating matchup against the No. 21 UCLA Bruins.

With the Ducks trailing the Bruins 17-9 in the fourth quarter, Lanning turned to Brock Thomas in hopes of sparking an offense that had struggled to move the football.

Oregon entered the contest ranked right outside the elite teams, but can't afford another loss. Yet that's what happened with Oregon falling to UCLA 17-15 on Saturday. Nevertheless, the Ducks found themselves in trouble without starting quarterback Dante Moore, who was unavailable after suffering a concussion against USC.

Moore's absence gave Raiola, a transfer from Nebraska, an opportunity to lead the offense following Oregon's bye week.

However, his performance against UCLA quickly became a major concern. Raiola completed just 6-of-19 passes for 43 yards and threw two interceptions. He also lost a fumble, contributing to Oregon's alarming turnover problems. Wide receiver Evan Stewart and running back Jordon Davison also fumbled, leaving the Ducks with six turnovers against the Bruins.

The decision to replace Raiola came after an offensive performance that fel well short of expectations. However, Thomas struggled to provide an immediate solution. On his first drive, he fumbled the snap from center lapani Laloulu on fourth down, resulting in another turnover.

The quarterback controversy is particularly notable because Raiola had impressed against USC. He completed 19-of-25 passes for 289 yards and two touchdowns, helping Oregon secure an important victory. That performance raised expectations, making his struggles against UCLA even more disappointing.

Now, attention turns to Oregon's upcoming matchup against Nebraska on Saturday, October 17. With Moore's return date still uncertain, Lanning must decide whether to give Raiola another opportunity, continue with Thomas, or prepare another option.

Ultimately, Oregon's biggest problem extends beyond the quarterback position. Six turnovers and an inability to sustain drives have exposed serious offensive issues. How Lanning addresses those problems could determine whether the Ducks recover quickly or face further questions about their championship ambitions.

articles.title: John Smoltz says quiet part out loud about Yankees’ playoff struggles
articles.summary: The New York Yankees fell short of winning the World Series once again this season. They were eliminated in the American League Division Series after getting...
articles.body:
The New York Yankees fell short of winning the World Series once again this season. They were eliminated in the American League Division Series after getting swept by the Tampa Bay Rays. New York hasn't won a World Series since 2009, and fans are growing impatient. Aaron Boone's job could be in question , but others simply believe New York needs to make offseason roster moves. Former MLB star pitcher and current broadcaster John Smoltz recently shared his thoughts on the Yankees' playoff struggles during an appearance on the Flippin' Bats Podcast.

"You also have to have the players that play Yankee baseball," Smoltz said. "And I don't know that there's a couple that play Yankee baseball. I thought their pitching and the way that they went about their roster was going to accomplish a lot more this year. Aaron Judge is a big piece, (Giancarlo) Stanton, all the different things that they rely on just weren't there at the end. And they're going to have to find an innovative way… I don't know if getting younger is the key."

The Yankees have been an incredibly successful regular season team over the years. That simply isn't good enough for a franchise that has 27 World Series championships, though. This current Yankees team is good — it just isn't good enough, especially factoring in the injuries that impacted the roster.

articles.summary: Vanderbilt football rolls over in a mistake-filled, cringeworthy blowout loss to Ole Miss.
articles.body:
Rapid reaction from Vanderbilt's 52-17 blowout loss to Ole Miss at FirstBank Stadium:

This Ole Miss team, favored by 9.5 points and ranked No. 11 (in the US LBM Coaches Poll), didn't need much help at Vanderbilt. But the Rebels got tons of it anyway from the Commodores , who piled up self-inflicted mistakes during an embarrassing opening half to fall behind 42-3. Among the lowlights: A pair of unnecessary post-play personal foul penalties, with the first likely halting a TD drive for the Commodores and the second extending a TD drive for Ole Miss after a third-down stop.

But, oh, it got worse: Vandy QB Jared Curtis, back from the hush-hush injury that sidelined him against Georgia, handed Ole Miss a touchdown with 43 seconds until halftime on a sack-fumble. And that wasn't even the Rebels' final points of the half. The Commodores fumbled the ensuing kickoff to gift another just 20 seconds later. That fumble was Curtis' fault. Not as much, though, when a first-half interception bounced off Junior Sherrill's hands and directly to an Ole Miss defensive back.

Vanderbilt's defense doesn't get a pass, either. It allowed Ole Miss to drive at least 54 yards for touchdowns on four consecutive possessions.

All the penalties and turnovers (not to mention the absence of any rushing threat in the game's first 20 minutes or so) never gave Vanderbilt a chance in a game decided well before halftime. Those mistakes, though, overshadowed some nice moments and throws by Curtis. He finished with 222 yards on 19-of-32 passing. Yes, there are signs of growth for the freshman QB. Didn't matter much on this day, but they will.

After Ole Miss went up 7-0 on its second possession, Vanderbilt's offense pushed back and would've had second-and-goal at the Rebels' 2 were it not for an unnecessary penalty foul penalty on Vandy offensive lineman Clinton Azubuike for getting salty after the first-down play. The Commodores ended up settling for a field goal. Those were their only points during the first half.

72 – Penalty yards for Vanderbilt in the first half alone. That was for seven penalties, not even including several on the Commodores that were declined. For the game, Vandy finished with 11 penalties for 92 yards.

Curtis can play. He's a freshman, and you'll definitely notice that inexperience and recklessness when you watch him play. But you'll see some big-time throws, too.

Vanderbilt's team isn't as hopeless as this game made it seem. But Vanderbilt isn't anywhere near good enough to play this poorly against a quality SEC opponent and not get embarrassed.

The worst part? This wasn't new. From the penalties and mental mistakes to the turnovers to an underwhelming run game, we'd seen all this already this season from Vanderbilt.

articles.title: Cal RB Ashten Emory scores 2 TDs in comeback win over Virginia Tech, 25-20
articles.summary: (AP) — Reserve running back Ashten Emory ran for two touchdowns and his 2-yard touchdown plunge with 18 seconds left capped Cal's 25-20 comeback win over Vir...
articles.body:
BERKELEY, Calif. (AP) — Reserve running back Ashten Emory ran for two touchdowns and his 2-yard touchdown plunge with 18 seconds left capped Cal's 25-20 comeback win over Virginia Tech on Saturday.

After trailing Virginia Tech for nearly the entire game, Cal (3-3, 2-1 Atlantic Coast Conference) went on a six-play, 75-yard drive to take the lead

Emory ran for 46 yards on 19 carries in relief of injured started Adam Mohammed due to a foot injury.

Following pre-game warmups, Cal quarterback Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele was ruled out due to a concussion he sustained during Cal's loss to UNLV last week. Jackson Brousseau replaced him, and the Colorado State transfer threw for 321 yards and one touchdown in his first start as a Golden Bear.

Both teams struggled to advance the ball in the first quarter, combining for just 81 yards of total offense.

The Hokies (4-2, 1-2) eventually got on the board first, when Ethan Grunkemeyer connected with Ayden Greene for a 30-yard touchdown pass in the second quarter. Two drives later, Cal put together a five-play, 85-yard drive that ended with a 5-yard scoring from Emory to tie it.

Marcellous Hawkins Jr.'s ran it in from 3 late in the second for a 14-7 Hokies lead. With 42 seconds left before halftime, Cal drove and converted a 35-yard field goal. The Bears added another field goal in the third.

Trailing 14-13, Brousseau led a drive late in the fourth, throwing a three-yard touchdown to Carson Perry-Smith to put the Golden Bears up 19-14. The Hokies responded with a nine-play, 73-yard drive of their own to regain the lead.

Down 20-19, Brousseau marched the Golden Bears down the field, Emory broke free off the edge and scored the game winner.

After missing the game-winning kick against Pittsburg last week, Virginia Tech kicker John Love was 0 for 2 on field goals, missing a 55-yarder in the first quarter and a 39-yarder in the fourth.

Virginia Tech: The Hokies' offense wasn't pretty. Meanwhile, the defense couldn't contain Cal's passing game and special teams. After starting 4-0, Virginia Tech has lost its last two games, both by one score.

Cal: The Golden Bears' offense was mostly one-dimensional, passing for 321 yards while rushing for just 82. But trailing late, Cal put the pieces together to pick up its second win in conference play.

Virginia Tech: Hosts Georgia Tech on Saturday.

articles.title: ALDS Game 5 thread: Cleveland Guardians vs. Chicago White Sox
articles.summary: Who will advance to battle the Rays for the pennant? Find out tonight in THE CLEVE.
articles.body:
This is definitely not a pretty playoff series. But I'll give it this: at least it's going the distance and providing us with baseball to fill the time between now and the League Championship Series. While the Braves and Padres folded in four to the Dodgers and Brewers, and the Yankees got unceremoniously dusted by the Rays, the Guardians fought back from down 0-2 and going on the road to win two in Chicago and force a decisive fifth game.

If the Guardos pull off the comeback, it'll be the first in the Division Series since the 2017 Yankees turned the trick at Cleveland's expense. It'll also be just the third ever in a best-of-five where the team lost the first two games at home, joining the 2001 Yankees and 2012 Giants. If the White Sox survive, however, then they'll play for their first pennant since 2005.

I'll just repeat what I said the other day about these two likely hapless teams: Yes, I'm hoping for a miracle in the ALCS and that one of these underwhelming AL Central teams can pull off an upset over Tampa Bay. Baseball's a silly sport. You never know! (I have far more hope in Cleveland making it a series than Chicago since I don't think the White Sox have any remotely rested pitchers, but we'll see what happens.

Cleveland Guardians vs. Chicago White Sox(winner-take-all)

articles.title: Michigan State's wild comeback falls short in OT loss to Illinois
articles.summary: After a furious fourth-quarter comeback, the Spartans went gutsy on a 2-point conversion try in OT but an incomplete pass left them short.
articles.body:
EAST LANSING — The boo birds came out, and then came a Bronx cheer. Until the fourth quarter, the biggest roar at Spartan Stadium came when the videoboard showed hall of fame basketball coach Tom Izzo, who walked through a sparse student section after halftime trying to rally the fans.

Those who stayed witnessed one heck of a comeback, but Michigan State couldn't finish it off in overtime for a win.

An early 17-point hole put Michigan State behind the ball against Illinois in front of a homecoming crowd at Spartan Stadium. A furious fourth-quarter comeback brought up overtime, and the Spartans went gutsy on a 2-point conversion try, but an incomplete pass left the Spartans short, 38-37, to extend its losing streak to four games.

On the first play of overtime, Illinois quarterback Michael Clayton II hit receiver Hudson Clement for a 25-yard touchdown. Michigan State receiver Chrishon McCray set the Spartans up 1 yard from paydirt, where a jumbo package look carved the way for Jaziun Patterson's third touchdown. On a 2-point try, quarterback Alessio Milivojevic took the ball off a trick play pitch and lofted a pass to Jayden Savoury, only for it to fall incomplete.

The result means Michigan State (2-4, 0-3 Big Ten) has lost 17 of its past 20 Big Ten games, where its offensive shortcomings and injuries on defense have glared. Against a similarly stumbling Illinois team, the Spartans started slow and missed out on a gamble for the win.

Up next, Michigan State will face Pat Fitzgerald's alma mater and former team, Northwestern, at Spartan Stadium Oct. 17 for a noon kickoff. Northwestern is off to a 4-1 start under quarterback Aidan Chiles, MSU's starter the past two seasons.

Another former MSU starter, Katin Houser, led an Illinois (3-3, 1-2) offense that picked apart the MSU defense in the first half. Houser threw 20-for-29 for 194 yards and a touchdown before leaving the game injured after throwing a pick to MSU safety Devin Vaught with 1:41 left in the third quarter.

After Patterson ran the remaining 11 yards to the end zone, he sparked a rally from 13 points down. It was Patterson who tied the game with 1:17 on the clock off a 2-yard rushing touchdown. It was Patterson who set up the game-deciding 2-point conversion with more overtime heroics.

Michigan State's offense didn't move the chains for a first down until 8:44 into the second quarter. Though the game began with successive three-and-outs that brought out boos, Milivojevic made a few big throws, including his first touchdown in three games.

A Brennan Parachek fumble ended MSU's first drive of the second half, which Illinois turned into a 38-yard field goal. Michigan State matched that on its next drive, a 40-yard kick by Liam Boyd set up by a 36-yard sprint from Patterson including a spin-move to break free.

Up 23-17 after Patterson's first touchdown, Illinois cushioned its lead when backup quarterback Clayton took advantage of two freshman cornerbacks for MSU and threw a 14-yard touchdown to Collin Dixon. Illinois went for two on the conversion, and Aidan Laughery got it on the second try to lead 31-17. But MSU kept chopping.

MSU got down to Illinois' 43 before facing fourth-and-2. A false start pushed it back, but Fredrick Moore caught the ball past the sticks to keep the offense moving. He caught the next pass for a 24-yard touchdown that got it back to a one-score game, 31-24.

True freshman Samson Gash grabbed the ensuing onside kick with 7:47 to play, only for an offsides flag to call the play back. Video replay showed he was onside, an unreviewable penalty, but officials reviewed his recovery and determined he caught it out of bounds to give Illinois the ball anyway.

But wait, there's more. The referee got on the mic once again to say that Gash caught it inbounds after all thanks to "additional video." Zapruder brought out the kick team once again, and Boyd just kicked it toward the end zone.

MSU stared at a 17-0 hole early after Houser led back-to-back touchdown drives and all four drives for scores in the first half. He threw a 5-yard touchdown to Laughery at 3:21 of the first quarter and scrambled in from 2 yards out at 8:57 of the second quarter after he previously overthrew a receiver.

For the first time in three games, starting linebackers Jordan Hall and Brady Pretzlaff played a drive together, and that gave MSU's defense a boost to start the game. Each of them left the game on the next series, Hall hurting his arm again and Pretzlaff landing funny on his neck. By the end of the game, backup Dion Crawford also left injured, straining the Spartans' depth.

articles.title: Indiana WR Nick Marsh gets monster props from Robert Griffin III
articles.summary: Indiana football escaped from the clutches of a Nebraska upset attempt in winning 20-17 Saturday. A Cornhuskers win would’ve snapped the Hoosiers’ 21-game w...
articles.body:
Indiana football escaped from the clutches of a Nebraska upset attempt in winning 20-17 Saturday . A Cornhuskers win would've snapped the Hoosiers' 21-game winning streak. IU has wide receiver Nick Marsh to thank, who drew love from Robert Griffin III .

The Heisman Trophy winning quarterback from Baylor raved about Marsh's game. He shouted out the wideout after delivering 187 yards, plus scoring the final two touchdowns for the Hoosiers.

Indiana was trailing by 11 before Marsh took the soul out of the Cornhuskers. And in the process silence the crowd that began to increase the decibel levels in Lincoln.

Head coach Curt Cignetti turned to the prized Michigan State transfer to prevent IU's historic streak from snapping. Marsh arrived as a prized transfer portal addition via the Big Ten rival Spartans. Many fans and analysts envisioned that Marsh would ignite this offense even further next to towering wideout Charlie Becker. Plus form immediate chemistry with new quarterback Josh Hoover, who was replacing prized Heisman Trophy winning passer Fernando Mendoza.

Marsh showed his game-breaking ability when Indiana needed it the most. Saturday marked his best performance yet in the Hoosiers uniform and kept the defending national champions unbeaten.

So Indiana's schedule gets rigid from here following the Nebraska contest. IU still has No. 5 ranked Ohio State coming back and best believe, the Buckeyes want revenge for losing out on winning the conference title last season. And another nationally-ranked foe comes to Bloomington in current No. 18 the USC Trojans, who head to Penn State for a Saturday evening showdown.
